newsitem.title: CONGO: Reuter reporters leave Zaire after expulsion threat.
newsitem.headline: Reuter reporters leave Zaire after expulsion threat.

text.p: Three Reuters journalists left Zaire on Saturday after their accreditations were withdrawn and they were threatened with expulsion.

The three crossed by boat to neighbouring Congo a day after Zaire's information minister, Kin-Kiey Mulumba, announced the government would deport immediately any foreign journalists without press accreditation.

The journalists were detained for two hours in Kinshasa on Thursday by the SNIP security police after they were told by an information ministry official without elaboration they had "breached the guidelines" for foreign media.

On Friday, Kin-Kiey, the government spokesman, renewed his attacks on media coverage of Zaire's civil war. "More than ever the war of Zaire is a media war," he said in a summary of Friday's cabinet meeting, broadcast on state television.

"The government has instructed the minister of interior and territorial security to escort immediately to the border foreign journalists whose accreditations have been withdrawn by the ministry of information," Kin-Kiey said.
The Reuter journalists are John Chiahemen, Nicholas Kotch and William Wallis. Wallis also works for the British Broadcasting Corporation.
Reuters photographer Howard Burditt also had his accreditation withdrawn but had already left the country before the Information Ministry acted.

More than 100 foreign journalists and television technicians are currently in the Zairean capital trying to report on the crisis. Every day for the past week a number of foreign journalists have been victims of assault, harassment or temporary detention by Zaire's security agencies.
